chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him)
That Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to accept the gifts (or stipends) of Mu'awiya.

key_terms.الْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, the second and third Imams
key_terms.جَوَائِزَ: Gifts or stipends given by the ruler
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةَ: Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, the Umayyad caliph

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams accept gifts from the Umayyad rulers?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the pragmatic political strategy of the Imams by accepting stipends from Mu'awiya, thereby avoiding the appearance of rebellion or financial independence that could be used as a pretext for their elimination. Scholars note that this acceptance was not merely a social courtesy but a calculated move to maintain their status and influence within the Umayyad court while preserving their religious authority. It underscores the distinction between accepting worldly provisions for survival and compromising core doctrinal principles.
